title: Ordinary and derived completion models for a fixed calculus
statement: For a prime l, finite extension E/Q_l, scheme W and any specified CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus S, there exists an ordinary quotient model M with a compatible DerivedModel S M. No residue-characteristic invertibility hypothesis is needed. Interfaces: [def-trf-completion-unit-models], [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

source.place: Tags 07A6, 0941, with derived.tex Tag 09T5 and sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7, 03EK; explicit strict quotient construction.

proof.text: Take the existing ordinary quotient tensor/limit adjunction. Its exact restriction and constant-tower limit have the normalized right-derived composition unit. Derive the tensor functor on the resolving class of flat-term K-flat complexes. Compare this left adjoint with the supplied S.reduction using uniqueness of adjoints to the same total limit. Transport its universal left-derived comparison and its Hom formula. The finite-adjunction mate calculation gives the finite reduction equation. The canonical termwise limit comparison, right-derived limit unit and strict Roos isomorphism supply the remaining fields. The construction is over the coefficient sheaf and does not use invertibility of l on W, boundedness, or completeness.

proof_origin.place: Derived quotient/limit adjunction and strict quotient system; P4 formal assembly, 2026-10-26.
